description: The chart represents the distribution of articles across various media outlets. The pie chart is divided into 17 slices, each representing a different media outlet. The slices are labeled with the names of the outlets, and some have percentage labels inside them. The proportions are as follows: Breitbart (blue) at approximately 14%, Other (gray) at 13%, Drudge Report (orange) and The Daily Caller (green) both at around 8%, The Huffington Post (red) at 7%, NPR (purple) and Vox (brown) both at 6%, The Guardian (pink) and BBC (tan) both at 5%, RT (yellow), Daily Kos (teal), National Review (blue), Daily Mail (pink), RedState (lavender), Fox News (light blue), CNN (red), PoliticusUSA (pink), and Shareblue (lavender) all at 3%. The chart does not include a legend, and some labels are placed outside the chart near their corresponding slices. The slices are arranged in a descending order of size, with the largest slice, Breitbart, being the most prominent.
